title: Multi-surface hosted endpoints PRD: scope clarifications, acceptance criteria, and launch rundown
creator: Priya Nair
description: This ticket captures the PRD and launch checklist for the consolidated hosted endpoints surface (chat, completions, embeddings, rerank). Goal is to finalize scope, acceptance tests, rollout gates, and post-launch monitoring so the product and engineering teams have a single source of truth for go/no-go decisions.
goals: Ship a single consistent hosted inference surface for devs covering chat, completions, embeddings, and rerank with unified auth, metrics, and error semantics
Ensure behavior parity with existing hosted lanes for common calls while enabling improved cost/latency defaults
Provide deterministic acceptance criteria and automated tests that block rollouts if metrics regress
out_of_scope: Dedicated/Dedicated-reserved capacity features (handled in Dedicated roadmap)
On-prem installation packaging and air-gapped deployment flows
Model training, model selection, or serving new architectures beyond the verified catalog (models accepted via separate onboarding flow)
user_stories: As a product engineer, I want a single REST surface that supports chat streaming and non-streaming so I can migrate code paths with minimal changes
As an ML infra engineer, I want deterministic latency and cost targets for embeddings so I can size pipelines and budgets
As an SRE, I want rollout gates with automatic rollback on QoS regressions to protect customer traffic
acceptance_criteria: API contract: endpoints accept documented params (messages/prompt, max_tokens, temperature, top_p, functions for chat) and return documented fields; schema validated by contract tests (PR integration)
Behavioral parity: 95% of sampling tests for existing canonical prompts must match baseline behavioral fingerprints within configured tolerance (unit suite: evals/hosted-surface/fingerprint-v1)
Latency SLOs: p95 latency for chat streaming start-of-stream < 120ms on default small prompt profile; p99 overall token latency < 350ms for chat on hosted tier
Embeddings throughput: batch worker must sustain 20k vectors/minute per pool node for the canonical 512-d model under typical load profile
Rerank correctness: top-1 precision measured on the graybox rerank test set must be within 1.5% of baseline model variant
Error surface: documented HTTP status codes and error body shape; all endpoints return consistent 4xx/5xx semantics and include stable error_code strings
Telemetry: every request must emit trace_id, model_variant, route, latency_ms, and token_count to the telemetry pipeline; ingest verified in staging dashboards
Security: keys and tokens validated; no plaintext customer data logged; security sign-off recorded (security_review_required=true)
rollout_plan: Stage 0 (internal): deploy to staging with full contract tests and synthetic traffic; run production-like evals for 48h
Stage 1 (canary-1): 1% traffic (non-paying demo tenants) for 24h; monitor functional tests and telemetry; manual review
Stage 2 (canary-2): 5% traffic (selected customers + internal org) for 48h; enforce automated gates: latency, error_rate, fingerprint drift
Stage 3 (ramp): 25% -> 50% over 72h if gates pass; enable fallthrough routing for degraded modeling
Stage 4 (global): full traffic; continue monitoring and open rollback window of 24h where automatic rollback can occur on regressions
monitoring_sla_metrics: consumer-facing request success rate (SLO target: 99.6% over 24h)
embedding throughput and queue depth metrics
engineering_notes: KV-cache behavior: chat streaming will use prefix-KV caching; decision: initial release will disable inter-request KV sharing across tenants to simplify privacy audits
Batching: embeddings service will expose a target_batch_size toggle; default auto-batching uses workload-aware heuristics from Optimize module
Fallthrough model policy: routing layer will mark lesser-quantized variants available for cost fallback; behavior contracts must be explicit in response.meta.fallback_reason
Signature: request signature and replay protection handled in control plane; engineering to add edge validation in ENG-6392
Compatibility: legacy hosted endpoints will remain available for 3 months post-cutover with migration docs and redirect guidance

2026-03-05: Design feedback incorporated — clarified streaming start-of-stream UX and error presentation. Added mockups to design_links.

launch_checklist: Contract test suite green in CI (PR + main) and deployed to staging
Synthetic eval harness executed with baseline fingerprint comparison (results uploaded to Confluence)
Canary pipeline configured with automated gates and rollback rules
Telemetry dashboards (canary/production) created and observed for 48h
Customer migration docs authored and reviewed by PM and Solutions (draft in Drive)
Security checklist completed (KMS keys, audit logging, data retention), SEC-1124 closed
Billing mapping validated for new endpoints and cost metrics emitted
Support runbook and escalation path documented with on-call rotations for first 7 days post-launch
Post-launch eval plan scheduled (7-day and 30-day quality reviews)
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: behavioral drift causes downstream product regressions. Mitigation: gated fingerprint tests and 0%->1% canary with manual hold points.
Risk: embeddings throughput shortfall under high concurrency. Mitigation: autoscaling policy and emergency burst capacity in Dedicated for heavy customers.
Risk: inconsistent error semantics between legacy and new endpoints. Mitigation: compatibility shim and a 3-month parallel support window.
Risk: security audit finds retention violations. Mitigation: explicit retention param default and audit by SEC team before Stage 2
post_launch_actions: Run 7-day quality/eval sweep and compare to baseline; escalate if drift > 3% on core prompts
Consolidate customer feedback and open follow-up PM tickets for UX tweaks and parameter defaults
Measure cost-per-1k-tokens and publish optimization recommendations for teams (Optimize playbook)
Schedule a retro with SRE, Eng, Design, Security at 14 days post-launch
